summary: Revision five (maintainer-directed) keeps the round-four scope, EDC.4 with the twelve EDC.6 interfaces that accepted packets import by id, and applies the maintainer's generality rule. Weak Lefschetz is now stated for bounded constructible complexes on a separated finite-type scheme, for any closed subscheme with affine complement and any of the finite, integral and rational coefficient regimes, with compact-support, supported (Gysin), integral p⁺ and Galois-equivariant forms; Deligne's smooth projective statement, its Gysin and integral refinements and the ample-divisor form are its corollaries. A new node gives Katz's weak Lefschetz for generic affine hyperplane sections. Affine vanishing extends to perfections, complete-intersection cohomology to families, the projective-bundle formula to flag bundles and section classes, and the vanishing and restricted subspaces to any smooth divisor. The round consumes the open TauCetiRoadmap pull requests EtaleCohomologyFoundations (#938), EnhancedDerivedSheaves (#908), ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology (#875), ComplexComparisonPartII (#848), LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (#873), DeligneWeightsAndPurity (#929) and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons (#965), and SchemeAndStackFoundations on main; the axis blow-up of a pencil is retired to LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles. No gap remains in this packet.

nodes.title: Artin vanishing for constructible complexes on affine schemes
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, n ≥ 1 invertible in k, Λ a noetherian ring with nΛ = 0, and U an affine scheme of finite type over k. (a) Imported, not planned here: for every constructible sheaf F of Λ-modules on U_ét, H^q(U, F) = 0 for q > dim Supp F (Artin's affine vanishing with the support-sensitive bound; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.affineArtinVanishing). (b) Let K ∈ D^b_c(U, Λ) and let d_q ∈ ℤ ∪ {−∞} satisfy dim Supp ℋ^q(K) ≤ d_q for every q (dim ∅ = −∞). Then H^m(U, K) = 0 for every m > max_q (q + d_q). (c) In particular, if dim Supp ℋ^q(K) ≤ −q for all q, that is K ∈ pD^{≤0}(U), then H^m(U, K) = 0 for m > 0 (for perverse K this is the statement of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8, imported); and H^m(U, K) = 0 for m > dim U + max{q : ℋ^q(K) ≠ 0}. (d) The same bounds hold for K ∈ D^b_c(U, O_E) and D^b_c(U, E) (E/ℚ_ℓ finite, ℓ invertible in k). (e) Universal homeomorphisms: the bounds (a)–(d) hold for every affine scheme U′ with a universal homeomorphism U′ → U onto an affine U of finite type over k, supports being measured in |U′| = |U|. In particular they hold when k is perfect of characteristic p and U′ is an affine perfect k-scheme perfectly of finite presentation, for example the perfection of an affine k-scheme of finite type. Parts (b)–(e) are the complex, adic and perfect forms that the upstream section does not state.
hypotheses: k separably closed; n invertible in k; Λ noetherian with nΛ = 0 (for (a) and (b)).
U affine of finite type over k; affineness is essential: H²(P¹, Λ(1)) = Λ although dim P¹ = 1.

For O_E and E coefficients use EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.5: normalized ℓ-adic systems with cohomological and Tor intervals uniform in the level, their realization, and finite E/ℚ_ℓ through O_E lattices. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
For (e): U′ → U a universal homeomorphism with U affine of finite type over k; in the perfect case k is perfect of characteristic p and U′ is affine, perfect and perfectly of finite presentation.
proofSteps: (a) is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3 (VanishingCycles.affineArtinVanishing), which states the constructible bound q > dim Supp F for prime-to-characteristic torsion coefficients; it is the statement of SGA 4 XIV Théorème 3.1 and Corollaire 3.2, restated as BBD Corollaire 4.1.4.

(b) Use the hypercohomology spectral sequence E₂^{p,q} = H^p(U, ℋ^q K) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, K), which converges because K is bounded. By (a), E₂^{p,q} = 0 for p > d_q, so every term with p + q = m vanishes when m > q + d_q for all q.
(c) is (b) with d_q = −q, respectively d_q = dim U.

(d) For O = ℤ_ℓ, apply (b) to each level ℤ/ℓ^n of the normalized system (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.1). The universal-coefficient sequence puts the support of ℋ^q(K_n) inside the supports of ℋ^q(K) and ℋ^{q+1}(K), and q + d_{q+1} < (q+1) + d_{q+1}, so the levels satisfy the same bound max_q(q + d_q). Pass to the realization: §F.4.2 identifies RΓ of the realization with Rlim of the finite levels; the groups H^{m−1}(U, K_n) are finite (§F.3), so the Milnor lim¹ term vanishes and H^m(U, K) = 0 above the bound. For O = O_E restrict scalars to ℤ_ℓ; rational coefficients follow by inverting ℓ (§F.4.5). The bound is imposed only on nonzero ordinary cohomology sheaves.

(e) A universal homeomorphism induces an equivalence of étale sites transporting sheaves, supports and cohomology (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.4, VanishingCycles.universalHomeomorphismEtaleEquivalence; for perfections Zhu, Remark A.4 and Proposition A.5). An affine perfect k-scheme perfectly of finite presentation is the perfection of a k-scheme of finite presentation (Zhu, Definition A.13 and Proposition A.15), and that model is affine because affineness passes between a scheme and its perfection (Zhu, Lemma A.7(6)); apply (a)–(d) to the model.
acceptance: U = 𝔸¹_k, F constructible: H^q(𝔸¹, F) = 0 for q ≥ 2; the bound is sharp: for n > 1, H¹(𝔾_m, ℤ/n) ≅ ℤ/n(−1) ≠ 0.
K = i_{x*}Λ[−q] for a closed point x: d_q = 0, and H^m(U, K) = 0 for m ≠ q, as (b) predicts.
Non-example: U = P¹ is not affine and H²(P¹, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ, so affineness cannot be dropped.

Perfect case: over an algebraically closed k of characteristic p, the perfection Spec k[t^{1/p^∞}] of 𝔸¹ is not of finite type, yet it has H^q = 0 for q ≥ 2 with constructible coefficients, exactly as 𝔸¹ by (e).

nodes.title: Compact-support vanishing on affine schemes and its smooth lisse case
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, U an affine scheme of finite type over k and a ∈ ℤ, with coefficients as in the conventions (Λ finite with invertible annihilator, O = O_E, or E). (a) Imported, not planned here: H^i_c(U, P) = 0 for i < 0 for every perverse P on U; for O this holds in the p-heart and in the p⁺-heart (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8). (b) If K ∈ pD^{≥a}(U), then H^i_c(U, K) = 0 for i < a. For field coefficients (a finite field of characteristic ℓ, or E) the condition K ∈ pD^{≥a} is the dual support bound dim Supp ℋ^q(D_U K) ≤ −a − q for every q, the form used in Weil II 6.2.11 and in LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §7b.9 (InvariantCycles.dualSupportAffineVanishing, stated there for ℚ_ℓ on hyperplane complements and imported). (c) If Λ = O and K ∈ p⁺D^{≥a}(U), then H^i_c(U, K) = 0 for i < a and H^a_c(U, K) is a torsion-free O-module. (d) Smooth case: if U is smooth of pure dimension d and L is a locally constant constructible sheaf of Λ-modules (Λ finite), or a locally free lisse O- or E-sheaf, then L ∈ pD^{≥d}(U) and H^i_c(U, L) = 0 for i < d; for a locally free lisse O-sheaf also L ∈ p⁺D^{≥d}(U), so H^d_c(U, L) is torsion-free.
hypotheses: k separably closed; U affine of finite type over k. Affineness is essential: H⁰_c(P¹, Λ) = Λ ≠ 0 although Λ[1] is perverse on P¹.

Coefficient regimes: Λ a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k; O = O_E for a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ with ℓ invertible in k; or E. Perverse t-structures are the middle perversity of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure and, for O and E, of EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; for O the dual perversity p⁺ is that of EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity. These agree with VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.

For the duality steps, D_U = RHom(−, a^!Λ) for a : U → Spec k is the dualizing functor of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5; biduality holds on D^b_c for finite fields, DVR quotients O/λ^m, O and E. A finite ring Λ is reduced to self-injective ℤ/ℓ^m-coefficients by restriction of scalars, as in EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing.
proofSteps: (a) is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8 for finite and rational coefficients and both integral hearts; in the atlas it is the compact-support half of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing (BBD 4.1.1–4.1.2 with duality).

(b) Induct on the perverse amplitude of the bounded K. The triangle pτ^{≤b}K → K → pτ^{≥b+1}K and the long exact sequence of RΓ_c(U, −) reduce the claim to a single shifted perverse object P[−b] with b ≥ a, and H^i_c(U, P[−b]) = H^{i−b}_c(U, P) vanishes for i < b by (a), in particular for i < a. For field coefficients D_U exchanges pD^{≥a} and pD^{≤−a} (EDC.5/perverse-verdier-self-duality), and pD^{≤−a} is the support condition dim Supp ℋ^q ≤ −a − q (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure); this gives the dual support form.

(c) For P in the p⁺-heart, D_U P lies in the p-heart (EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity), so H^m(U, D_U P) = 0 for m > 0 by perverse Artin vanishing (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing). Duality for U → Spec k gives RΓ_c(U, P) ≅ RHom_O(RΓ(U, D_U P), O); as O has global dimension one, H^i_c(U, P) = 0 for i < 0 and H^0_c(U, P) = Hom_O(H^0(U, D_U P), O) is torsion-free. The truncation argument of (b) for p⁺ then gives H^i_c(U, K) = 0 for i < a and H^a_c(U, K) ≅ H^0_c(U, p⁺H^a(K)), which is torsion-free. EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8 states the same two facts for the hearts.

(d) For a locally constant constructible L on smooth U of pure dimension d, L[d] is perverse (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse, using smooth purity i_x^!L ≅ i_x^*L(−c)[−2c]), so L ∈ pD^{≥d} and (b) applies. For a locally free lisse O-sheaf, D_U(L[d]) = L^∨(d)[d] is again a shifted locally free lisse sheaf, hence p-perverse, so L[d] lies in the p⁺-heart as well and (c) applies.

Cross-check with Deligne's route (Weil II 4.1.6): for field coefficients and lisse L, Poincaré duality gives H^i_c(U, L) ≅ H^{2d−i}(U, L^∨(d))^∨, which vanishes for 2d − i > d by Artin vanishing (EDC.4/affine-vanishing-hypercohomology (a)). The residue-field dévissage of the fourth round remains a valid alternative for locally constant sheaves over self-injective finite rings; the perverse argument above makes it unnecessary.
acceptance: U = 𝔸^d: H^i_c(𝔸^d, Λ) = 0 for i ≠ 2d, in particular for i < d.
U = 𝔾_m (d = 1): H⁰_c(𝔾_m, Λ) = 0 while H¹_c(𝔾_m, Λ) = Λ ≠ 0 for nonzero Λ — the bound i < d is sharp.
Non-example: U = P¹ is not affine and H⁰_c(P¹, Λ) = Λ ≠ 0 although d = 1.

A complex that is not a shifted local system: on U = 𝔸¹ with j : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹, K = j_!Λ[1] is perverse; H^i_c(𝔸¹, K) = H^{i+1}_c(𝔾_m, Λ) vanishes for i < 0, and H⁰_c(𝔸¹, K) ≅ Λ, so (b) is sharp for a = 0.

The p⁺ hypothesis in (c) is needed: on U = Spec k with O-coefficients, the p-perverse torsion object O/λ has H⁰_c = O/λ, which is torsion; its dual (O/λ)[−1] lies in the p⁺-heart and has H⁰_c = 0 and torsion H¹_c = O/λ, so torsion-freeness is asserted in degree a only.

nodes.title: The weak Lefschetz theorem for complexes
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, X a separated scheme of finite type over k, i : Y → X a closed subscheme whose complement j : U → X is affine, n ∈ ℤ, and K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ) for a coefficient regime of the conventions (Λ finite with invertible annihilator, O = O_E, or E). (a) If j^*K ∈ pD^{≥n+1}(U), the restriction H^q_c(X, K) → H^q_c(Y, i^*K) is bijective for q < n and injective for q = n; when X is proper these are the ordinary groups H^q(X, K) → H^q(Y, i^*K). (b) Dually, if j^*K ∈ pD^{≤n+1}(U), the forgetful map H^q_Y(X, K) → H^q(X, K) is bijective for q > n + 2 and surjective for q = n + 2. (c) If Λ = O and j^*K ∈ p⁺D^{≥n+1}(U), the cokernel of H^n_c(X, K) → H^n_c(Y, i^*K) is a torsion-free O-module. (d) If X, Y and K come from X₀, Y₀ and K₀ over a subfield k₀ with k = k₀^sep, the maps of (a)–(c) are Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant; over k₀ = 𝔽_q they commute with the geometric Frobenius. (e) Classical case: let X be smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1, Y = X ∩ H for a hyperplane H of a projective embedding containing no irreducible component of X (Y need not be smooth), and L a locally constant constructible Λ-sheaf (Λ finite) or a locally free lisse O- or E-sheaf. Then L ∈ pD^{≥n+1}(X), so H^q(X, L) → H^q(Y, i^*L) is bijective for q < n and injective for q = n. Imported, not planned here: for a smooth ample hyperplane section and constant coefficients this is VanishingCycles.etaleWeakLefschetz of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7, and for ℚ_ℓ-complexes on a projective X with Y a hyperplane section, (a) under the equivalent dual support bound is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §7b.9. This node adds the finite and integral coefficient regimes, arbitrary closed subschemes with affine complement in a separated X, the compact-support and supported forms (a)–(c) and the equivariance (d).
hypotheses: k separably closed; X separated of finite type over k; U = X − Y affine. The affineness of U is the only property of Y that is used; for a hyperplane section of a projective X it holds because U is closed in P^N − H ≅ 𝔸^N.

Coefficient regimes: Λ a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k; O = O_E for a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ with ℓ invertible in k; or E. Perverse t-structures are the middle perversity of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure and, for O and E, of EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; for O the dual perversity p⁺ is that of EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity. These agree with VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
For field coefficients K ∈ pD^{≥n+1} is equivalent to the dual support bound dim Supp ℋ^q(DK) ≤ −n − 1 − q of Weil II 6.2.11 and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §7b.9.

This theorem is distinct from hard Lefschetz (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9) and makes no claim about the nondegeneracy of the intersection form on the vanishing part (EDC.4/vanishing-and-restriction-subspaces).
For (d), K₀ is a bounded constructible complex on X₀ whose pullback is K; the Frobenius conventions are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b.
proofSteps: Affineness in the classical case: U = X − Y → P^N − H is a closed immersion, hence an affine morphism (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_iff_isAffineHom), into the affine scheme P^N − H = D_+(h) ≅ Spec of a degree-zero localization (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec); so U is affine (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isAffine_of_isAffineHom).

(a) The localization triangle j_!j^*K → K → i_*i^*K (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.7, ClassicalAlgebraic.supportLocalization) and compact supports (§§0.8, F.2.5) give the exact sequence … → H^q_c(U, j^*K) → H^q_c(X, K) → H^q_c(Y, i^*K) → H^{q+1}_c(U, j^*K) → …. By EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine (b), H^q_c(U, j^*K) = 0 for q < n + 1. Hence restriction is injective for q ≤ n and surjective for q ≤ n − 1. For proper X, compact and ordinary cohomology agree on X and on the closed Y.

(b) The triangle i_*i^!K → K → Rj_*j^*K gives … → H^{q−1}(U, j^*K) → H^q_Y(X, K) → H^q(X, K) → H^q(U, j^*K) → …. Perverse Artin vanishing on the affine U (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing) gives H^m(U, j^*K) = 0 for m > n + 1, hence surjectivity for q ≥ n + 2 and injectivity for q ≥ n + 3.
(c) In the sequence of (a), the cokernel of H^n_c(X, K) → H^n_c(Y, i^*K) injects into H^{n+1}_c(U, j^*K), which is torsion-free by EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine (c).

(d) All maps are induced by morphisms of schemes and complexes defined over k₀, hence commute with the Galois action (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.6, VanishingCycles.adicFunctoriality, and §F.10.2b, VanishingCycles.frobeniusCohomology).
(e) L[n+1] is perverse on the smooth X (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse), so L ∈ pD^{≥n+1}(X), and j^* is t-exact; apply (a) with X proper.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n a hyperplane: i^* : H^q(P^{n+1}, Λ) → H^q(P^n, Λ) is an isomorphism for q ≤ 2n (the P^m calculation of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9), consistent with the theorem.
X = P¹ × P¹ ⊂ P³ (n + 1 = 2), Y a smooth conic: i^* is injective on H¹ = 0 and an isomorphism on H⁰; on H² (outside the range) the map Λ(−1)² → Λ(−1) is not injective, so the range q ≤ n is sharp.
n + 1 = 1 (X a smooth projective curve, Y a finite set of points): H⁰(X) → H⁰(Y) is injective.

Agreement with the upstream statement: for Y smooth and L = Λ constant, the conclusion is that of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7 (VanishingCycles.etaleWeakLefschetz), whose plane-cubic check H¹(P²) = 0 → H¹(C) = Λ² is injective and not surjective.

Singular ambient space: for the projective cone X ⊂ P³ over a smooth conic (a quadric surface with one singular point, a local complete intersection), Λ_X[2] is perverse, so restriction to a hyperplane section Y missing the vertex is bijective on H⁰ and injective on H¹; smoothness of X is not used.

(b) in the smooth case: for X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n and K = Λ, purity identifies H^q_Y(X, Λ) with H^{q−2}(P^n, Λ(−1)), and H^{q−2}(P^n)(−1) → H^q(P^{n+1}) is bijective for q > n + 2 and surjective for q = n + 2.

nodes.title: The dual (Gysin) form of weak Lefschetz
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, X a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type of pure dimension n + 1, and i : Y → X a smooth closed subscheme of pure dimension n (a smooth effective Cartier divisor) whose complement U is affine, for instance a smooth hyperplane section of a smooth projective X. Let L be a locally constant constructible Λ-sheaf (Λ finite) or a locally free lisse O- or E-sheaf. Then the Gysin map i_* : H^q(Y, i^*L) → H^{q+2}(X, L(1)) is bijective for q > n and surjective for q = n. Equivalently H^{q+2}(X, L(1))/i_*H^q(Y, i^*L) injects into H^{q+2}(U, L(1)), which vanishes for q + 2 > n + 1. If X, Y and L are defined over k₀ with k = k₀^sep, the Gysin map is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant, and over 𝔽_q it commutes with the geometric Frobenius.
hypotheses: As stated; X need not be proper: the argument uses only the localization triangle, smooth-pair purity and the affineness of U.

Coefficient regimes: Λ a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k; O = O_E for a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ with ℓ invertible in k; or E. Perverse t-structures are the middle perversity of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure and, for O and E, of EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; for O the dual perversity p⁺ is that of EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity. These agree with VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: L[n+1] is perverse on the smooth X (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse), so L(1) ∈ pD^{≤n+1}(X); EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (b) applies to K = L(1).

Smooth-pair purity identifies i^!L(1) ≅ i^*L[−2] (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.10, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothBoundaryPurity, and its adic form in §F.6, VanishingCycles.smoothPairGysin), so H^{q+2}_Y(X, L(1)) ≅ H^q(Y, i^*L) and the forgetful map becomes the Gysin map i_*. EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (b) gives bijectivity for q + 2 > n + 2 and surjectivity for q + 2 = n + 2.

For field coefficients and proper X this is the transpose of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (e) under Poincaré duality on X and Y (the Gysin map is the transpose of i^*, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6), which gives the same ranges.
Equivariance as in EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (d); the Gysin map raises the twist by one.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n: i_* : H^q(P^n) → H^{q+2}(P^{n+1})(1) sends h^j to h^{j+1}; it is an isomorphism for n < q ≤ 2n and surjective for q = n.
n = 0: Y a finite set of d ≥ 1 distinct geometric points on a smooth connected projective curve X; i_* : H⁰(Y) = Λ^d → H²(X, Λ(1)) = Λ is the sum map, surjective.
The range is sharp: for X = P¹ × P¹ and Y a conic, i_* : H⁰(Y) → H²(X)(1) is not surjective onto Λ² (q = 0 < n = 1).

Agreement with DeligneWeightsAndPurity §9.3(c) (open pull request #929): for a smooth hyperplane section of a smooth projective X and ℚ_ℓ-coefficients the dual Gysin statement there is this conclusion.

sources.match: Deligne states the Gysin (dual) form of weak Lefschetz.
Weil I uses the surjectivity of the Gysin map H^{n−1}(Y)(−1) → H^{n+1}(X) as the dual of weak Lefschetz.

§0.10 states smooth-pair purity i^!Λ ≅ Λ_Z(−c)[−2c] with its class, and §F.6 the Gysin maps of smooth pairs with their projection formulas and adic realizations; with the triangle of §0.7 they give the Gysin sequence used here.

States, for a smooth hyperplane section of a smooth projective variety and ℚ_ℓ-coefficients, that the Gysin map is the transpose of restriction and the dual Gysin form of weak Lefschetz; used here as the rational agreement check.

nodes.title: Integral weak Lefschetz: torsion-freeness of the cokernel
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz with Λ = O = O_E: if j^*K ∈ p⁺D^{≥n+1}(U), then H^{n+1}_c(U, j^*K) is a torsion-free O-module and so is the cokernel of H^n_c(X, K) → H^n_c(Y, i^*K). In particular (Weil II 4.1.6), for X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1, Y = X ∩ H a hyperplane section and U = X − Y, the group H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is torsion-free and H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/i^*H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ) is torsion-free; the same holds with ℤ_ℓ replaced by O_E or by any locally free lisse O-sheaf L on X.
hypotheses: k separably closed, ℓ invertible; X separated of finite type over k with U = X − Y affine; for the classical case X smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1 and Y a hyperplane section.

The integral perversity p⁺ is the dual of p (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity). A locally free lisse O-sheaf L on a smooth X of pure dimension n + 1 satisfies L ∈ p⁺D^{≥n+1}, because D(L[n+1]) = L^∨(n+1)[n+1] is p-perverse.

RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is a perfect complex of ℤ_ℓ-modules with RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ ≅ RΓ_c(U, ℤ/ℓ): this is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.4 (VanishingCycles.adicFiniteness). O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: General case: EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (c), whose torsion-freeness input is EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine (c).

Deligne's route for K = ℤ_ℓ, kept as a cross-check: since RΓ_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) is perfect with derived reduction RΓ_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.4), there is a short exact sequence 0 → H^n_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) ⊗ ℤ/ℓ → H^n_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) → Tor₁^{ℤ_ℓ}(H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ), ℤ/ℓ) → 0. The middle term vanishes by EDC.4/compact-support-vanishing-smooth-affine (d) (n < n + 1), so H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) has no ℓ-torsion, and a finitely generated ℤ_ℓ-module without ℓ-torsion is torsion-free.
The exact sequence H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ) → H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ) → H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ) of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz embeds H^n(Y)/i^*H^n(X) into the torsion-free H^{n+1}_c(U, ℤ_ℓ).
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}: H^{n+1}_c(𝔸^{n+1}, ℤ_ℓ) = 0 (torsion-free) and the cokernel H^n(P^n)/H^n(P^{n+1}) = 0.
X a smooth projective surface (n = 1) with Y a smooth hyperplane curve: H¹(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/i^*H¹(X, ℤ_ℓ) is a free ℤ_ℓ-module (the vanishing part of the curve's H¹ is saturated).

Affineness diagnostic: U = P¹ is smooth of dimension one but non-affine, and H⁰_c(U, ℤ/ℓ) = ℤ/ℓ ≠ 0. Thus smoothness alone does not supply the compact-vanishing input used by the universal-coefficient argument.
p⁺ cannot be replaced by p: for X = U = Spec k, Y = ∅ and n = −1, the p-perverse torsion object O/λ has H⁰_c = O/λ, which is torsion.

sources.match: Deligne's (4.1.6): the universal coefficient formula gives the torsion-freeness of H^{n+1}_c(X − Y, ℤ_ℓ), hence of H^n(Y, ℤ_ℓ)/H^n(X, ℤ_ℓ).

States finite generation over ℤ_ℓ, bounded perfect RΓ and RΓ_c, and the derived reduction RΓ_c(X, K_ℤℓ) ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ^n ≅ RΓ_c(X, K_n) for separated finite-type schemes over a separably closed field; this is the hypothesis of the first step.

nodes.title: Weak Lefschetz for ample divisors and hypersurface sections
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, X a proper k-scheme, ℒ an ample invertible O_X-module, r ≥ 1 and s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ^{⊗r}) with zero scheme Y = V(s). Then U = X − Y = X_s is affine, so EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (a)–(d) apply to (X, Y) and to every K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ) with j^*K ∈ pD^{≥n+1}(U), for Λ finite, O or E. In particular, if X is smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1 and s is nonzero on every irreducible component (so Y is an effective Cartier divisor), restriction H^q(X, L) → H^q(Y, L) is bijective for q < n and injective for q = n for every locally constant constructible or locally free lisse L, and when Y is smooth the Gysin statement of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin holds. This applies to Y = X ∩ V(F) for a homogeneous form F of degree r on P^N ⊃ X, and by induction along a chain X = X_0 ⊃ X_1 ⊃ … ⊃ X_c of smooth successive ample divisors.
hypotheses: X proper over k separably closed; ℒ ample; Y the zero scheme of a section of a positive power of ℒ. For the statements about local systems X is smooth projective of pure dimension n + 1 and the section is nonzero on every irreducible component, so Y is an effective Cartier divisor.

Only the affineness of X − Y = X_s is used beyond EDC.4/weak-lefschetz, together with topological invariance of the étale site (Y and Y_red have the same cohomology; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.4).
proofSteps: X is proper over k and ℒ^{⊗r} is ample, so X_s = X − Y is affine (Stacks, Tag 0EKE: for f universally closed and ℒ f-ample, X_s → S is affine; requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0). Ampleness alone does not suffice without properness: on a quasi-affine non-affine X with ℒ = O_X and s = 1, X_s = X.
With U = X_s affine, EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (a)–(d) and EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin apply verbatim: they use only the affineness of the complement.

Hypersurface sections: the degree-r Veronese embedding (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §3.4, LefschetzPencil.veronese with veronese_isClosedImmersion and veronese_hyperplane) turns V(F) ∩ X into a hyperplane section of the re-embedded X (Weil I, 5.7), whose complement is affine by the argument of EDC.4/weak-lefschetz.
Chains: apply the statement to each X_{j+1} ⊂ X_j (each smooth projective) and compose.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y a smooth quadric hypersurface (r = 2): H^q(Y) ≅ H^q(P^{n+1}) for q < n.
n + 1 = 2, X = P², Y a smooth plane cubic curve: H⁰(P²) → H⁰(Y) is an isomorphism (q = 0 < n = 1) and H¹(P²) = 0 → H¹(Y) = Λ² is injective.

Non-example: take X = P¹ × P¹ and ℒ = O(0,2), nef but not ample, with s vanishing at two distinct points of the second factor. Then Y is the disjoint union of two fibres and H⁰(X,Λ) = Λ → H⁰(Y,Λ) = Λ² is diagonal, not an isomorphism although 0 < n = 1. The complement P¹ × G_m is non-affine and H¹_c(P¹ × G_m,Λ) = Λ ≠ 0, violating the low-degree compact vanishing required in the proof.

For X proper (universally closed) and ℒ ample, X_s is affine: the complement of an ample divisor in a proper scheme is affine.
States that universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of étale sites with transport of sheaves and cohomology; used to replace Y by its reduction.

nodes.title: Weak Lefschetz for generic affine hyperplane sections
nodes.statement: Let k be a separably closed field, V a separated scheme of finite type over k, π : V → 𝔸^N a quasi-finite morphism, and P a perverse complex on V for a coefficient regime of the conventions (Λ finite with invertible annihilator, O with the perversity p, or E). For (a, b) ∈ k^N × k put H_{a,b} = {Σ a_i x_i + b = 0} ⊂ 𝔸^N, V_{a,b} = π^{−1}(H_{a,b}) with closed immersion ι_{a,b}, and let j_{a,b} : V − V_{a,b} → V be the open complement. There is a dense open 𝒰 of the parameter space 𝔸^{N+1} of affine maps 𝔸^N → 𝔸¹ such that for (a, b) ∈ 𝒰(k): (1) H^q(V, j_{a,b!}j_{a,b}^*P) = 0 for q < 0; (2) the restriction H^q(V, P) → H^q(V_{a,b}, ι_{a,b}^*P) is bijective for q < −1 and injective for q = −1. (3) If V is smooth of pure dimension d ≥ 1 and F is a locally constant constructible Λ-sheaf (Λ finite) or a locally free lisse O- or E-sheaf, then H^q(V, F) → H^q(V_{a,b}, F) is bijective for q < d − 1 and injective for q = d − 1; if moreover V is connected and d ≥ 2, then V_{a,b} is nonempty and connected. (4) If V is smooth and irreducible of dimension d ≥ 2 and π is unramified, then V_{a,b} is smooth and irreducible of dimension d − 1 for (a, b) in a dense open. Iterating (3) and (4) along successive generic affine hyperplanes H_1, H_2, … ⊂ 𝔸^N gives smooth connected sections V ∩ H_1 ∩ … ∩ H_i of dimension d − i with the same restriction ranges at each step.
hypotheses: k separably closed; V separated of finite type; π quasi-finite. For (4), V smooth irreducible and π unramified.

Coefficient regimes: Λ a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k; O = O_E for a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ with ℓ invertible in k; or E. Perverse t-structures are the middle perversity of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure and, for O and E, of EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; for O the dual perversity p⁺ is that of EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity. These agree with VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8. O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the perversity conditions, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
The open 𝒰 depends on V, π and P; nothing is asserted for special hyperplanes: (a, b) = (0, 0) gives the whole of V and (0, b) with b ≠ 0 the empty section.

Katz states (1)–(3) for ℚ̄_ℓ-coefficients and, in (3), for local complete intersections V of pure dimension d, where F[d] is perverse; this node plans the smooth case, in which the perversity of F[d] is EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse.
proofSteps: Reduction to projective space: put K := Rπ_*P on 𝔸^N and K̄ := Rι_*K for the open immersion ι : 𝔸^N → P^N. Quasi-finite direct images are left t-exact (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/quasi-finite-perverse-exactness), so K̄ ∈ pD^{≥0}(P^N), and H^q(V, P) = H^q(P^N, K̄).

Generic base change: by generic local acyclicity of the universal hyperplane family over the dual projective space (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.genericLocalAcyclicity, applied to the incidence family pulled back along the smooth projection to P^N, §F.2.2; for ℚ̄_ℓ-complexes this is LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §7b.7, InvariantCycles.genericHyperplaneRestriction), there is a dense open of hyperplanes H̄ ⊂ P^N on which restriction to H̄ commutes with Rι_*Rπ_* and with extension by zero from the complement. Remove the hyperplane at infinity and identify the remaining open with an open 𝒰 of the space of affine maps; for (a, b) ∈ 𝒰(k), K̄|_{H̄} computes RΓ(V_{a,b}, ι^*P).

Weak Lefschetz on projective space: P^N is proper and P^N − H̄ ≅ 𝔸^N is affine, so EDC.4/weak-lefschetz (a) with n + 1 = 0 gives H^q(P^N, K̄) → H^q(H̄, K̄|_{H̄}) bijective for q < −1 and injective for q = −1. By the previous step this is (2). The triangle j_!j^*P → P → ι_*ι^*P shows that (2) is equivalent to (1).

(3) For smooth V of pure dimension d, F[d] is perverse (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse); apply (2) to P = F[d]. When d ≥ 2, H⁰(V, F) → H⁰(V_{a,b}, F) is bijective, which for F = Λ and connected V gives a nonempty connected section.

(4) is the Bertini input requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 (Katz, Lemma 3.5): for smooth irreducible V and unramified π the parameters with smooth (d − 1)-dimensional section contain a dense open; with the connectedness of (3) this gives irreducibility (Katz, Corollary 3.4.3).
Iteration: apply (3) and (4) to V ∩ H_1 inside H_1 ≅ 𝔸^{N−1} and continue (Katz, Sums of Betti numbers, Theorem 8).
acceptance: V = 𝔸² with π the identity and F = Λ: a generic line V_{a,b} ≅ 𝔸¹ is connected and H^q(𝔸²) → H^q(𝔸¹) is bijective for q = 0 and injective for q = 1.

Sharpness at q = d − 1: for V = 𝔸² − C with C a smooth affine conic (characteristic not two), H¹(V, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1) by the Gysin sequence, while a generic line meets C in two points and H¹(V_{a,b}, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1)²; restriction is injective and not surjective.
Special parameters are excluded: for π the identity of 𝔸², (a, b) = (0, 0) gives V_{0,0} = V and (0, 1) gives the empty section; neither lies in 𝒰.
Agreement with the source: for ℚ̄_ℓ-coefficients and smooth V, (3) is Katz's weak Lefschetz (Affine cohomological transforms, Corollary 3.4.1), and (1)–(2) are his Theorem 3.4 with f = 0.

nodes.title: Cohomology of smooth complete intersections
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, ℓ invertible in k, and X ⊂ P^N_k a smooth complete intersection of dimension m ≥ 1 (there is a chain P^N = X_N ⊃ X_{N−1} ⊃ … ⊃ X_m = X with each X_r = X_{r+1} ∩ H_r for a hypersurface H_r, all X_r smooth). Let Λ = ℤ/ℓ^a, ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ and h = c₁(O(1))|_X ∈ H²(X, Λ(1)). Then: (a) for q ≠ m, 0 ≤ q ≤ 2m, H^q(X, Λ) = 0 for q odd and H^q(X, Λ(q/2)) is free of rank one for q even; h^{q/2} generates for q < m. For q > m, a generator is dual to h^{m−q/2} under Poincaré duality, and h^{q/2} is deg(X) times that generator (after the trace normalization); the restriction H^q(P^N, Λ) → H^q(X, Λ) is an isomorphism for q < m. (b) H^m(X, Λ) = Λ(−m/2)·h^{m/2} ⊕ H^m(X, Λ)_0 when m is even (for Λ = ℚ_ℓ, and for ℤ/ℓ^a or ℤ_ℓ when deg X is prime to ℓ), with H^m(X)_0 := ker(∪h : H^m(X) → H^{m+2}(X)(1)); H^m(X) = H^m(X)_0 when m is odd. (c) With ℤ_ℓ coefficients all H^q(X, ℤ_ℓ) are torsion-free. (d) If X is defined over 𝔽_q, the geometric Frobenius acts on H^{2j}(X, ℚ_ℓ), 2j ≠ m, by multiplication by q^j. The comparison of primitive ranks across characteristics is the separate target EDC.6/complete-intersection-betti-comparison; it is not a conclusion of this node. (e) Families: let S be a scheme on which ℓ is invertible and f : X → S a smooth projective morphism whose geometric fibres are smooth complete intersections of dimension m ≥ 1 and fixed multidegree in P^N, embedded in P^N_S with relative hyperplane class η ∈ H⁰(S, R²f_*Λ(1)). For Λ = ℤ/ℓ^a and 0 ≤ q ≤ 2m with q ≠ m, R^qf_*Λ = 0 for q odd, and for q even R^qf_*Λ(q/2) is the constant sheaf Λ_S, generated by η^{q/2} for q < m and by the section dual to η^{m−q/2} under the relative trace pairing for q > m; R^mf_*Λ is locally constant constructible, and for m even with the degree prime to ℓ it splits as Λ_S(−m/2)·η^{m/2} ⊕ ker(∪η). The same holds for the ℤ_ℓ- and ℚ_ℓ-systems (R^qf_*ℤ/ℓ^a)_a. Over S = Spec k₀ the constant sheaves Λ_S(−q/2) give back the Galois and Frobenius statements of (d).
hypotheses: X a smooth complete intersection in P^N over a separably closed field; ℓ invertible.
The splitting in (b) uses that h^m has degree deg X on X (Tr(h^m) = deg X): it is a direct sum over ℚ_ℓ, and over ℤ/ℓ^a or ℤ_ℓ only when deg X is a unit.

For (e): S any scheme with ℓ invertible; f smooth projective with a relative embedding in P^N_S and geometric fibres smooth complete intersections of dimension m ≥ 1 and fixed multidegree; the relative trace is that of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11 for smooth separated finitely presented f.
proofSteps: Induction along the chain X_N = P^N ⊃ … ⊃ X_m = X, each X_r an ample divisor in the smooth projective X_{r+1} (EDC.4/ample-divisor-weak-lefschetz): H^q(X_{r+1}) → H^q(X_r) is bijective for q < r and injective for q = r; the Gysin map H^q(X_r)(−1) → H^{q+2}(X_{r+1}) is bijective for q > r and surjective for q = r (EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-gysin).

Hence H^q(X) ≅ H^q(P^N) for q < m, where H^*(P^N) has one Λ(−i) in each even degree 2i generated by the hyperplane powers (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 and the first check of §F.7), and by Poincaré duality on X (§§F.5–F.6, with the adic realization of §F.4.4) H^q(X) for q > m is dual to H^{2m−q}(X), which is Λ·h^{m−q/2} or 0.

Torsion-freeness: for each smooth divisor X_r in X_{r+1}, integral weak Lefschetz (EDC.4/weak-lefschetz-integral) gives an injection H^r(X_{r+1}, ℤ_ℓ) → H^r(X_r, ℤ_ℓ) with torsion-free cokernel. The source group is in a degree below dim X_{r+1}, hence identified with the free projective-space group by the already proved low-degree calculation. Therefore the middle group of X_r is free as well. Integral Poincaré duality and its universal-coefficient sequence then give freeness in all higher degrees, including degree r+1. This avoids assuming freeness in degree r+1 to prove it in degree r.

Splitting (b): Tr_X(h^m) = deg X (the degree of the hyperplane class on X, from the point normalization of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 and the projection formula of §F.6), so h^{m/2} ∪ h^{m/2} ≠ 0 and Λh^{m/2} is a direct summand complementary to the kernel of ∪h when deg X is invertible in Λ.

Frobenius: the low-degree hyperplane powers have eigenvalue q^j in untwisted cohomology (geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(1) by q⁻¹, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b). In high degrees use the perfect Frobenius-equivariant pairing with low degrees, whose multiplier is q^m; the resulting eigenvalue is q^j even when h^j is not an integral generator.

(e) By smooth and proper base change each R^qf_*Λ is locally constant constructible with geometric stalks H^q(X_s̄, Λ) (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.lisseDirectImageTransport), computed by (a)–(c). The global section η^{q/2} of R^qf_*Λ(q/2) generates every stalk for q < m, so Λ_S → R^qf_*Λ(q/2) is an isomorphism. For q > m, the relative trace R^{2m}f_*Λ(m) → Λ_S (§0.11) and cup product give a pairing R^qf_*Λ(q/2) ⊗ R^{2m−q}f_*Λ(m − q/2) → Λ_S that is perfect on stalks by Poincaré duality on the fibres, so R^qf_*Λ(q/2) ≅ Λ_S. The splitting of R^mf_*Λ is the stalkwise splitting of (b), defined by global sections. Over S = Spec k₀ a constant sheaf Λ(−j) has geometric Frobenius eigenvalue q^j, which is (d).
acceptance: X = P^m itself (N = m): H^m(X)_0 = 0 and every statement reduces to the P^m calculation of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9.
X a smooth plane cubic (m = 1): H¹(X, ℚ_ℓ) = H¹(X)_0 has dimension 2 = b_1^0 for degree 3.
X a smooth quadric surface in P³ (m = 2, degree 2): H²(X, ℚ_ℓ(1)) = ℚ_ℓh ⊕ H²_0 with dim H²_0 = 1; with ℤ/2 coefficients the splitting fails (deg X = 2 is not invertible), as the hypothesis requires.
Smooth plane conic with Λ = ℤ/2: H²(X, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ but h = 2[point] = 0. With ℤ₂, h spans an index-two submodule. Thus high-degree freeness must not be stated as generation by h.

The active forms are typed over the common finite-type separated k-base; the carrier data for ample sections and complete-intersection chains are the SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 requests of this packet.

Quadric family: for a smooth quadric f : X → S of relative dimension m (degree 2), R^{2i}f_*ℤ_ℓ(i) is constant, generated by η^i for 2i < m and by η^i/2 for m < 2i ≤ 2m; this agrees with the smooth-quadric calculation of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §2.3 (open pull request #873).

Agreement with LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §4.5, Application (hypersurfaces outside the middle degree, ℚ_ℓ-coefficients): for a smooth hypersurface the groups outside degree m are those of projective space, as (a) states.

nodes.title: The projective-bundle decomposition: ring structure, pushforward, pairing and Frobenius weights
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and Λ a finite ring annihilated by an integer n invertible on X (by derived extension of scalars from ℤ/n, as in EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9), with bounded constructible K. For Λ = O_E or E require additionally that X is of finite type over a field with ℓ invertible and take bounded constructible K. Let V be a locally free O_X-module of rank m + 1, π : P(V) → X the projective bundle of lines in V and ξ = c₁(O(1)) ∈ H²(P(V), Λ(1)). (a) Imported, not planned here: the map ⊕_{j=0}^{m} Λ_X(−j)[−2j] → Rπ_*Λ_{P(V)} given by ξ^j is an isomorphism (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9, ClassicalAlgebraic.cycleClasses, for finite Λ; its adic realization is §F.7); consequently, by the projection formula, H^q(P(V), π^*K) ≅ ⊕_j H^{q−2j}(X, K(−j)) for every such K. The node adds: (b) ring structure: ⊕_q H^q(P(V), Λ(∗)) = H^∗(X, Λ(∗))[ξ]/(Σ_{r=0}^{m+1} c_r(V) ξ^{m+1−r}); (c) for X smooth over k and π_* the Gysin pushforward (relative dimension m), π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^j) = 0 for j < m and π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^m) = a; (d) if X and V are defined over a field k₀ and k = k₀^sep, the decomposition H^q(P(V)_k, Λ) ≅ ⊕_j H^{q−2j}(X_k, Λ)(−j) is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant; over k₀ = 𝔽_q the geometric Frobenius acts on the j-th summand as F_X ⊗ q^j (untwisted cohomology); (e) for X smooth proper of pure dimension d over k separably closed, the Poincaré pairing on P(V) restricted to the summands j and j' vanishes when j + j' < m and is ⟨π^*a ξ^j, π^*b ξ^{m−j}⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩_X when j + j' = m. (f) Complete flag bundles: for V of rank r ≥ 2 let φ : Fl(V) → X be the complete flag bundle, built as the tower of projective bundles P(V) ← P(Q_1) ← … with tautological lines and ξ_i the class of the dual of the i-th tautological line. Then H^*(Fl(V), Λ) is a free H^*(X, Λ)-module on the monomials ξ_1^{a_1}⋯ξ_{r−1}^{a_{r−1}} with 0 ≤ a_i ≤ r − i, φ^* is split injective in every degree, and φ^*V carries the tautological filtration by subbundles with line-bundle quotients whose first Chern classes x_1, …, x_r satisfy φ^*c_k(V) = e_k(x_1, …, x_r) (the splitting principle; the Whitney formula is that of EDC.3/chern-classes). (g) Zero and infinity sections: for a line bundle L and V = O_X ⊕ L (m = 1) the sections P(O_X) and P(L) of P(V) → X are disjoint divisors with cl(P(L)) = ξ and cl(P(O_X)) = ξ + π^*c₁(L); their product vanishes, which is the relation ξ² + π^*c₁(L)ξ = 0 of (b).
hypotheses: X qcqs with n invertible and Λ a finite ℤ/n-algebra (for (c) and (e): X smooth, respectively smooth proper, over a field); V locally free of rank m + 1 (Zariski-locally free); for (f) V of rank r ≥ 2.

P(V) parametrizes lines in V and ξ = c₁(O(1)), with O(1) dual to the tautological line: this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.4 (projectiveBundle V := relativeProj of the symmetric algebra of V^∨, with projectiveBundle_dual_convention) on TauCetiRoadmap main; the plus-sign Chern relation follows this convention.
Twists and Frobenius conventions are those of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.3 (etaleTateTwists) and §F.10.2b (geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(−1) by q).

The étale Chern classes c_r(V) of (b) are those of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/chern-classes (defined by the projective-bundle relation); EtaleCohomologyFoundations states c₁ (§0.9) but not the higher étale classes. The adic extension is the realization of §F.7 in its finite-type range; O_E-coefficients are regarded as ℤ_ℓ-coefficients with an O_E-action along the finite free ℤ_ℓ → O_E; this changes neither the cohomology groups, nor the supports, nor the maps, and a finitely generated O_E-module is O_E-torsion-free exactly when it is ℤ_ℓ-torsion-free.
proofSteps: (a) is imported: EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9 states the decomposition for finite Λ with summands generated by powers of c₁(O(1)), compatibly with pullback and coefficient reduction, and §F.7 realizes it adically through §F.4. The cohomological form with coefficients π^*K follows from the projection formula (§F.2.7 for Rf_! = Rf_* along the proper π).
(b) is the definition of the Chern classes by the projective-bundle relation (EDC.3/chern-classes) together with the freeness in (a).

(c) The pushforward π_* along the smooth proper π is the trace of Rπ_! = Rπ_* against π^!Λ ≅ Λ(m)[2m] (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11 and smooth purity, §F.6), and the projection formula (§F.2.7) gives π_*(π^*a ∪ ξ^j) = a ∪ π_*(ξ^j); π_*(ξ^j) ∈ H^{2j−2m}(X) vanishes for j < m by degree and π_*(ξ^m) = 1 because on a fibre P^m, Tr(ξ^m) = 1 (point normalization of §0.9).

(d) ξ is the Chern class of a line bundle defined over k₀, so it is Galois-invariant in H²(P(V)_k, Λ(1)); in untwisted cohomology F^*ξ = q·ξ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.10.2b: geometric Frobenius acts on Λ(1) by q⁻¹), which gives the stated action.
(e) Tr_{P(V)} = Tr_X ∘ π_* (compatibility of smooth traces with composition, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothTrace), and (c).

(f) Iterate (a) and (c) along the tower of projective bundles of the tautological quotients (Grothendieck 1958, §1): each stage multiplies the basis by the powers ξ_i^a with a at most its relative dimension, and the pushforward of the top power splits each pullback. The tautological sub-line bundles give the filtration of φ^*V; its Chern-root identity is the Whitney formula of EDC.3/chern-classes applied to the filtration.

(g) P(L) is the zero scheme of the composite of the tautological inclusion O(−1) → π^*V with the projection to π^*O_X, a section of O(1); P(O_X) is the zero scheme of O(−1) → π^*L, a section of O(1) ⊗ π^*L. Each section is regular, and the class of the zero scheme of a regular section of a line bundle is its first Chern class (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9, Cartier-divisor agreement). The two sections are disjoint, so the product of their classes is zero.
acceptance: X = Spec k for k separably closed, E = k^{m+1}: P(E) = P^m and (a) is H^∗(P^m) = Λ[ξ]/(ξ^{m+1}) (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9).

P¹-bundle over a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over 𝔽_q: the geometric Frobenius has eigenvalues those of H^a(C) and q times those of H^{a−2}(C) on H^a(P(E)); e.g. dim H²(P(E)) = 2 with eigenvalues q, q.
The Frobenius twist on the summand j is q^j, not 1: 'equal Betti numbers' is not enough (the stage forbids merely equating Betti numbers).

Agreement with the upstream statement: on a rank-one bundle P(V) = X and only the j = 0 summand occurs, and the zero bundle has empty projectivization, as in the checks of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9.
(f) For V of rank 3 over a separably closed point, Fl(V) is the flag variety of k³; the six basis monomials 1, ξ_1, ξ_2, ξ_1², ξ_1ξ_2, ξ_1²ξ_2 give Betti numbers 1, 2, 2, 1.
(g) Over X = Spec k with L trivial, P(V) = P¹ and both sections are points of class ξ, so ξ² = 0, as the relation with c₁(L) = 0 requires.

nodes.title: Direct images along the blow-up of a smooth centre
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, ℓ invertible in k, X a smooth separated finite-type k-scheme, i : Z → X a smooth closed subscheme of pure codimension c ≥ 2, π : X̃ = Bl_Z X → X the blow-up, E = π^{−1}(Z) the exceptional divisor with j : E → X̃ and p = π|_E : E → Z, and ζ := c₁(O_E(1)) = −j^*c₁(O_X̃(E)) ∈ H²(E, Λ(1)). Then X̃ is smooth, E is a smooth divisor with E ≅ P(N_{Z/X}) over Z (imported), Λ_X → Rπ_*Λ_X̃ is split injective, and Rπ_*Λ_X̃ ≅ Λ_X ⊕ ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a]; equivalently π_*Λ = Λ, R^{2a}π_*Λ ≅ i_*Λ_Z(−a) for 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 (generated by the image of ζ^a under j^*), and R^qπ_*Λ = 0 for all other q > 0. Λ is a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k, O_E or E. The splitting is the actual sum of the adjunction unit and j_*(zeta^(a-1)p^*(-)); its restriction to E has columns 1,-zeta,...,-zeta^(c-1).
hypotheses: X smooth, separated and of finite type over a field k, Z ⊂ X smooth of pure codimension c ≥ 2; ℓ invertible in k.

The geometry of the blow-up (X̃ smooth, E = P(N_{Z/X}), O_X̃(−E)|_E = O_E(1), π an isomorphism over X − Z, π proper) is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0. TauCetiRoadmap main states blow-ups and strict transforms (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.11 with StableReduction Layer 4) and normal bundles of regular immersions (§5.5), but not this identification of the exceptional divisor.
proofSteps: Over X − Z, π is an isomorphism, so Rπ_*Λ|_{X−Z} = Λ.

π is proper, so proper base change (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.2.1, VanishingCycles.properBaseChange) gives (R^qπ_*Λ)_z̄ = H^q(P^{c−1}_{z̄}, Λ) at geometric points z̄ of Z: Λ(−a) for q = 2a ≤ 2(c − 1), 0 otherwise (EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a) over a point).

Use the adjunction unit for Λ_X and, for 1 ≤ a ≤ c−1, the morphism i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a] → Rπ_*Λ_X̃ obtained from p^*, multiplication by ζ^{a−1}, and the exceptional-divisor Gysin map j_* (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, VanishingCycles.smoothPairGysin). Their direct sum defines the proposed decomposition morphism.

Check this morphism on geometric stalks by proper base change. Off Z it is the identity. Over Z its restriction to E has columns 1 and −ζ^a, since j^*j_*y = −ζ∪y by the self-intersection formula of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6. These form the projective-bundle basis, so the morphism is an isomorphism. The trace π_* splits its first column by the degree-one projection formula. Merely knowing the cohomology sheaves of a complex would not prove a derived splitting.

Applying RΓ recovers VanishingCycles.etaleBlowup of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7, which states the decomposition of RΓ(Bl_Z X, Λ) with the same exceptional Gysin columns; this node is its sheaf-level form over X, needed for supports and compact supports in EDC.4/pullback-injective-blowup-bundle.
acceptance: Blow-up of a point in a surface (c = 2): R²π_*Λ = Λ_x(−1) at the point x, generated by the class of the exceptional curve.
c = 3, Z a point in a threefold: R²π_*Λ = Λ_x(−1), R⁴π_*Λ = Λ_x(−2), R¹ = R³ = 0.
Non-example: for c = 1 the blow-up is an isomorphism and Rπ_*Λ = Λ; the formula's sum over 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 is then empty, so no correction term appears.
The active forms are typed over the common finite-type separated k-base; the exceptional-divisor geometry is the SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 request of this packet.

nodes.title: The blow-up formula along a smooth centre: retraction, traces and Frobenius weights
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.4/blowup-direct-images, for every q the map Φ : H^q(X, Λ) ⊕ ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} H^{q−2a}(Z, Λ(−a)) → H^q(X̃, Λ), (x, (z_a)) ↦ π^*x + Σ_a j_*(ζ^{a−1} ∪ p^*z_a), where j_* : H^{r}(E, Λ(s)) → H^{r+2}(X̃, Λ(s+1)) is the Gysin map of the divisor E, is an isomorphism; this decomposition with its displayed exceptional Gysin columns and inverse signs is VanishingCycles.etaleBlowup of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7, imported. The node adds the following compatibilities of this specific Φ: its inverse has first component π_* (the Gysin pushforward, with π_*π^* = id); j^*π^*x = p^*i^*x; π_*j_*(ζ^{a−1} ∪ p^*z) = 0 for 1 ≤ a ≤ c − 1 (degree reasons along the fibres P^{c−1}); for X proper over k separably closed, Tr_X̃(π^*x) = Tr_X(x) on top-degree classes; if X, Z are defined over k₀ (k = k₀^sep) Φ is Gal(k/k₀)-equivariant and over 𝔽_q the geometric Frobenius acts on the summand H^{q−2a}(Z)(−a) as F_Z ⊗ q^a (untwisted). Λ is a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible in k, O_E or E.
hypotheses: As in EDC.4/blowup-direct-images; for Galois and Frobenius statements X and Z are defined over k₀ and the cohomology is that of X_k, Z_k.
For cohomology over a non-separably-closed k₀ the decomposition is of Galois modules after base change to k.
proofSteps: Apply RΓ(X, −) to Rπ_*Λ_X̃ ≅ Λ_X ⊕ ⊕_a i_*Λ_Z(−a)[−2a] (EDC.4/blowup-direct-images): H^q(X̃) ≅ H^q(X) ⊕ ⊕_a H^{q−2a}(Z)(−a). This is the decomposition stated by EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7.

Retain the imported exceptional Gysin columns of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.7. At the sheaf level EDC.4/blowup-direct-images identifies their exceptional restrictions as −ζ^a p^*; this supplies the comparison before applying any support functor. No second global blow-up decomposition is planned.

nodes.title: Pullback along blow-ups and projective bundles is split injective
nodes.statement: Let σ : X' → X be either (i) the blow-up of a smooth k-scheme X along a smooth closed subscheme Z of pure codimension c ≥ 2, or (ii) a projective bundle P(E) → X of relative dimension r ≥ 1 over a qcqs X, or (iii) the complete flag bundle Fl(E) → X of a vector bundle E of rank s ≥ 2 over a qcqs X, with ℓ invertible. For Λ a finite ring whose annihilator is invertible, O_E or E, σ^* : H^q(X, Λ) → H^q(X', Λ) is split injective, with retraction π_* in case (i), a ↦ σ_*(ξ^r ∪ −) in case (ii) and the iterated pushforward of the top monomial ξ_1^{s−1}ξ_2^{s−2}⋯ξ_{s−1} in case (iii); the same holds for cohomology with compact supports and for cohomology with supports in a closed subset T ⊂ X and its preimage. In case (ii) the cokernel is the sum of H^{q−2j}(X, Λ)(−j) for 1≤j≤r; for r=1 this is H^{q−2}(X, Λ)(−1), and in case (i) the cokernel is ⊕_{a=1}^{c−1} H^{q−2a}(Z, Λ)(−a), so σ^* is bijective in degrees q < 2 (and an isomorphism in all degrees when Z = ∅).

For compact supports assume X separated of finite type over a field, so RΓ_c is the supplied structural lower-shriek functor. The blow-up case retains that same geometric range from blowup-direct-images; the finite-coefficient ordinary/support projective-bundle statement keeps the qcqs range.

(ii) EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a) and (c).

Compact supports and supports in T: apply the same decompositions of Rσ_*Λ (EDC.4/blowup-direct-images, EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition (a)), which are isomorphisms in D(X, Λ), to RΓ_c(X, −) and RΓ_T(X, −); for σ proper, Rσ_! = Rσ_* (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.8, ClassicalAlgebraic.properSupports) and supports in the preimage of T are computed by the triangles of §0.7.

nodes.title: Vanishing and restricted subspaces of a smooth divisor, and primitive subspaces
nodes.statement: Let k be separably closed, ℓ invertible, E a field of coefficients (finite of characteristic ℓ, or finite over ℚ_ℓ), X a smooth proper k-scheme of pure dimension n + 1 and i : Y → X a smooth effective Cartier divisor (pure dimension n), with class L = c₁(O_X(Y)) ∈ H²(X, E(1)); the principal case is a smooth hyperplane section of a smooth projective X, with L = c₁(O_X(1)). Define the vanishing subspace Van(Y) := ker(i_* : H^n(Y, E) → H^{n+2}(X, E(1))) and the restricted subspace Res(Y) := im(i^* : H^n(X, E) → H^n(Y, E)), both E-subspaces of H^n(Y, E). Then, with respect to the Poincaré pairing ⟨y, y'⟩ = Tr_Y(y ∪ y') on H^n(Y, E) (perfect and (−1)^n-symmetric after the identification E(n) ≅ E over k), Res(Y) = Van(Y)^⊥ and Van(Y) = Res(Y)^⊥; dim Res(Y) + dim Van(Y) = dim H^n(Y). Moreover i_*i^* = L ∪ − on H^∗(X). For 0 ≤ q ≤ n + 1 the primitive subspace is P^q(X) := ker(L^{n+2−q} : H^q(X, E) → H^{2n+4−q}(X, E(n+2−q))). No decomposition H^n(Y) = Res(Y) ⊕ Van(Y) and no Lefschetz decomposition into primitive parts is asserted: both require hard Lefschetz (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9).
hypotheses: X smooth proper of pure dimension n + 1 over k separably closed; Y a smooth effective Cartier divisor (for instance a smooth hyperplane section); field coefficients E (so that orthogonal complements have complementary dimensions). Ampleness of Y is not used.
proofSteps: Van(Y) and Res(Y) are kernels and images of E-linear maps between finite-dimensional spaces (finiteness: EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.etaleFiniteness, for finite fields of coefficients; §§F.4.4–F.4.5 for ℓ-adic fields).

i_* is the transpose of i^* for the Poincaré pairings of Y and X (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, Gysin maps and their projection formula): ⟨i^*x, y⟩_Y = ⟨x, i_*y⟩_X. Hence y ⊥ Res(Y) ⟺ i_*y ⊥ H^n(X) ⟺ i_*y = 0 (perfectness of Poincaré duality on X, §§F.5–F.6), i.e. Res(Y)^⊥ = Van(Y); the pairing on Y is perfect, so Van(Y)^⊥ = Res(Y) and the dimensions add up.

i_*i^*x = cl(Y) ∪ x = L ∪ x (projection formula of §F.6 and the agreement of the class of a Cartier divisor with the Kummer first Chern class of O_X(Y), §0.9). Ampleness plays no role in these three steps.
P^q(X) is a kernel of an E-linear map; nothing about its complement is claimed.
acceptance: X = P^{n+1}, Y = P^n: Van(Y) = 0 for n odd (H^n(Y) = 0) and for n even Van(Y) = 0 since i_* is an isomorphism H^n(P^n) → H^{n+2}(P^{n+1}); Res(Y) = H^n(Y).
Take X = P² with its O(3) Veronese embedding and Y a smooth plane cubic, which is a hyperplane section for that embedding. Then Res(Y)=0 and Van(Y)=H¹(Y), of dimension 2.

The intersection Res(Y) ∩ Van(Y) is not asserted to be 0: in characteristic ℓ coefficients E = 𝔽_2 and n even, the restricted class of a quadric hyperplane section can be isotropic; only orthogonality is proved.

The P², O(3) test uses the actual degree-three Veronese embedding of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §3.4 (LefschetzPencil.veronese). Orthogonality uses the actual restriction/Gysin maps, not arbitrary subspaces with matching dimensions.

nodes.title: Classical and pro-étale ℓ-adic constructible categories
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a field (or over ℤ[1/ℓ]-regular bases of dimension ≤ 1), ℓ invertible on X, E/ℚ_ℓ finite with ring of integers O and uniformizer λ. Imported, not planned here: for O = ℤ_ℓ, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.1–F.4.6 state the normalized bounded constructible ℓ-adic systems (VanishingCycles.normalizedAdicSystems), their classical realization K_ℤℓ = Rlim K_n (VanishingCycles.classicalAdicRealization), the comparison Rν_*K_pro ≅ K_ℤℓ with the pro-étale realization (VanishingCycles.etaleProetaleAdicComparison), integral finiteness and derived reduction (VanishingCycles.adicFiniteness), rational and finite-E realization through O_E lattices (VanishingCycles.rationalAdicRealization), and the passage of proper, smooth and Rf_! exchange, projection, tensor and Künneth through normalized systems (VanishingCycles.adicFunctoriality); §F.5 states adic duality as the realization of the finite-level duality. The node adds the λ-adic form for a possibly ramified O: the category D^b_c(X, O), obtained by taking the homotopy category of the normalized full subcategory of the enhanced coefficient-system limit of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5, with K_m ∈ D_ctf(X, O/λ^m) and homotopy-coherent derived reduction equivalences (EDC.6/normalized-adic-system) is equivalent to Bhatt–Scholze's D_cons(X_proét, O) of derived λ-complete objects whose reductions are constructible, compatibly with the reduction functors K ↦ K ⊗^L O/λ^m. D^b_c(X, E) := D^b_c(X, O) ⊗ E is the full subcategory D_cons(X_proét, E), and D^b_c(X, Ē) is the 2-colimit over finite E'/E. Both carry the six operations f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f^!, ⊗, RHom, compatible with the finite-level ones under reduction and with coefficient extension E → E'; for O = ℤ_ℓ these are the imported operations.
hypotheses: X of finite type over a field (or a regular base of dimension ≤ 1) with ℓ invertible; E/ℚ_ℓ finite.

For the six operations use the hypotheses of Bhatt–Scholze §§6.6–6.7 and Remark 6.8.15: noetherian finite-dimensional bases with ℓ invertible, and the quasi-excellence hypothesis of 6.7.1 for nonproper direct image. Completion and coefficient reconstruction on a replete topos are EnhancedDerivedSheaves E4 (§E4.5); constructibility, boundedness and the scheme six operations are additional inputs, not consequences of repleteness alone.

Tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change are the enhanced operations of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3 in the ambient unbounded derived category; finite Tor amplitude is tested there against all degree-zero sheaves. Bounded outputs require actual bounded-constructible restriction witnesses. General-ring trace evaluation uses ctf inputs; bounded duality on every Dbc object uses its stated coefficient regime.

Use the enhanced limit and all higher coherence of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E4.5, taking its homotopy category only afterwards. For O = ℤ_ℓ this is EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4.2–F.4.3; for ramified O the same argument applies to the tower O/λ^m, since O/λ^{em} is a finite free ℤ/ℓ^m-algebra (e the ramification index) and the realization, its Milnor sequence and the pro-étale comparison only use the uniform bounds and the finite-level operations.

Six operations on D^b_c(X, O): defined levelwise on normalized systems by the finite-level operations of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.7–0.8, F.2 and F.5, which preserve D_ctf and commute with ⊗^L O/λ^m (projection formula, §F.2.7; finiteness, §F.3); E and Ē by localization and colimit (Bhatt–Scholze 6.8; for finite E also §F.4.5).

nodes.title: Transport of traces, duality and Gysin classes to ℓ-adic and rational coefficients
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, for X separated of finite type over a field k. Imported, not planned here: for O = ℤ_ℓ and for ℚ_ℓ and finite E, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5 states adic duality as the realization of finite-level duality, §F.6 the adic realizations of the smooth trace, purity and Gysin maps, §F.4.4 finite generation and derived reduction of geometric cohomology, and §F.4.5 rational tensor, Hom and duality. The node states these for a possibly ramified O = O_E and records the integral details used downstream: (a) the dualizing complex K_X := a^!O ∈ D^b_c(X, O) reduces to the finite-level K_X ⊗^L O/λ^m and D_X := RHom(−, K_X) preserves D^b_c(X, O); the evaluation K → D_XD_XK is an isomorphism for all K ∈ D^b_c(X, O) (its reductions have finite Tor amplitude over O/λ^m, so the imported ctf biduality applies levelwise and passes to the limit) and for D^b_c(X, E); D_X exchanges Rf_* and Rf_!, f^* and f^!. (b) The smooth trace Tr_f, the purity isomorphism f^!O ≅ O(d)[2d] for smooth f of relative dimension d, the Gysin maps and the cycle class map cl : CH^r(X) → H^{2r}(X, O(r)) are the limits of their finite-level versions, with integral torsion retained: for geometric cohomology (X over a separably closed field), H^q(X, O) = lim H^q(X, O/λ^m) is a finitely generated O-module whose torsion is not discarded, and the universal-coefficient sequences 0 → H^q(X, O) ⊗ O/λ^m → H^q(X, O/λ^m) → H^{q+1}(X, O)[λ^m] → 0 hold. The inverse-limit, finite-generation and finite-group Mittag-Leffler assertions in (b) concern geometric cohomology over a separably closed field. Cycle-class transport uses the perfect-field and cycle hypotheses of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/cycle-class-map, whose descent to Chow groups EtaleCohomologyFoundations does not state.
proofSteps: Use ambient coefficient reduction and the uniform ordinary/Tor bounds of the enhanced normalized systems for the bounded restrictions. O is a DVR of global dimension one: bounded constructible O-complexes are stratumwise perfect, and their derived reductions lie in D_ctf(X,O/λ^m) with a common interval. Apply exactly the ctf biduality and exchange isomorphisms of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5 at those levels; the dual systems retain common constructibility and bounds, and enhanced reconstruction gives integral biduality. Quotient-to-quotient reduction is not bounded on every Dbc object. No biduality on arbitrary nonperfect finite-level Dbc inputs is imported. Finite-group Mittag–Leffler is used only for geometric cohomology.

Traces, purity and Gysin maps are compatible with reduction by construction (their finite-level constructions in EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11 and F.6 are natural in Λ), hence define maps of systems; cycle classes likewise (EDC.3/cycle-class-map).

The finiteness clause is geometric; over arbitrary k the absolute Galois cohomology need not be finitely generated.
Coefficient extension: E' is finite free over E, so all operations commute with − ⊗_E E'.

nodes.title: Perverse t-structures with ℓ-adic coefficients and coefficient extension
nodes.statement: For X of finite type over k (ℓ invertible) and E/ℚ_ℓ finite, the middle perverse t-structure of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure on D^b_c(X, E) and on D^b_c(X, Ē) := 2-colim_{E'} D^b_c(X, E') is compatible with coefficient extension: for a finite extension E ⊂ E', K ↦ K ⊗_E E' is t-exact, induces an exact functor Perv(X, E) → Perv(X, E'), commutes with j_!* and IC (IC_X(L) ⊗_E E' ≅ IC_X(L ⊗_E E')), and Hom_{Perv(X,E')}(K ⊗ E', L ⊗ E') = Hom_{Perv(X,E)}(K, L) ⊗_E E'. Reduction from O to O/λ (K ↦ K ⊗^L O/λ) is right t-exact for p and sends the heart of p to pD^{[−1,0]} (EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity). Simple objects of Perv(X, Ē) are defined over some finite E'.
hypotheses: X of finite type over a field, ℓ invertible; E ⊂ E' finite extensions of ℚ_ℓ.

The perverse t-structures are those of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure (stated upstream as VanishingCycles.fieldPerverseTStructure, EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.8, for finite and ℓ-adic coefficients). The Hom scalar-extension identity is for a finite coefficient-field extension (general algebraic extensions through the stated filtered colimit), not an arbitrary field homomorphism.
proofSteps: Faithfully flat finite scalar extension commutes with stalks and costalks and is exact, hence perverse t-exact. It commutes with images in the heart, so commutes with j_!* and IC without using the special standard-truncation formula. The algebraic-closure case is the filtered union of finite coefficient extensions.
Homs: RHom commutes with the finite free extension (EDC.6/adic-transport-of-duality-and-classes).
Reduction: K ⊗^L O/λ sits in the triangle K →λ K → K ⊗^L O/λ →, whose perverse cohomology sequence gives the amplitude [−1, 0].
acceptance: IC_X(Ē) of a smooth curve is Ē[1].
For X = Spec Ω, ⊗E' is the scalar extension of finite-dimensional vector spaces.

nodes.title: Comparison with the complex-analytic constructible category
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over ℂ, X^an its analytification and Λ a finite ring (killed by n), O_E or E. Imported from ComplexComparisonPartII §§C6.3–C6.6: finite ordinary and compact Artin comparison, proper Rf_* exchange, separated Rf_! exchange on ctf inputs, and normalized ℤ_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ topological realization. The residue here is the categorical and perverse form, ramified O_E coefficients, the rational essential image, and the additional nonproper Rf_* exchange requested below. The comparison functor ε^* : D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) → D^b_c(X^an, Λ) (constructible for algebraic stratifications) is an equivalence for finite Λ (BBD 6.1.2, from Artin's comparison theorem SGA 4 XVI 4.1), commutes with f^*, Rf_*, Rf_! and f^! in their constructible ranges for morphisms of finite type. Tensor and RHom comparison are stated in the ambient unbounded categories: for bounded constructible K,L, finite Tor amplitude of K gives bounded-constructible restriction receipts for K⊗^L L and RHom(K,L), and the comparisons then restrict through these receipts. Bounded Verdier duality on every Dbc object is asserted only for the finite-field, DVR-quotient, integral and rational coefficient regimes; for a general finite ring it uses the existing ctf input range. The functor is t-exact for the middle perverse t-structures, so it identifies Perv(X_ét, Λ) with algebraically constructible perverse sheaves on X^an and preserves j_!* and IC. For O_E coefficients the corresponding equivalence follows from finite-level comparison. For E coefficients the functor is fully faithful with essential image the algebraically constructible complexes whose cohomology local systems on normal connected strata admit monodromy-stable O_E lattices (BBD 6.1.2(A″),(B″)); it is an equivalence onto that image; the comparison of trace maps and cycle classes with topological orientation classes is EDC.6/trace-orientation-comparison.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; algebraically constructible complexes; Λ finite, O_E or E.

For E coefficients the analytic target is restricted to the monodromy-stable-lattice essential image. A rank-one E local system on ℂ× with monodromy ℓ admits no stable O_E lattice and is not the analytification of an étale E local system.

Tensor and internal-Hom outputs are first ambient objects. A bounded output is corestricted only with its actual bounded-constructible witness; the displayed comparisons use finite-Tor first input. Analytic complex-field tensor/RHom used by geometric-origin constructors has separate field-coefficient boundedness receipts.
proofSteps: Import analytification and the finite/adic ordinary and compact comparisons from ComplexComparisonPartII §§C−1.1,C6.0–C6.6 (TauCetiRoadmap #848, head d6cb0fc). Its generic enhanced analytic categories use EnhancedDerivedSheaves §§0.1–0.4. It already supplies proper Rf_* and separated Rf_! exchange on ctf inputs. Request only the remaining nonproper constructible Rf_* comparison through SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2. BBD 6.1.2, pp.148–151 supplies the categorical refinement: finite and integral equivalences and rational full faithfulness with the stable-lattice essential image. Apply the finite comparisons levelwise to the coherent λ-adic systems for ramified O_E.

For the finite non-ctf coefficient range, use BBD 6.1.2(C),(C′),(C″), pp.148–151 and its localization/dévissage argument to extend the operation comparison beyond the imported ctf exchange. Rf_! is computed by proper pushforward and j_! using the existing Nagata compactifications. Define the f^! exchange by adjunction; compute it locally via smooth purity and closed/open localization as in BBD p.151. Do not infer it solely from global full faithfulness of ε^*.
Perverse t-exactness: the stalk/costalk conditions are computed on points of X and stratifications, which agree on both sides.

Realize Dbc in the unbounded coefficient category appropriate to its regime and AnalyticDbc in the native derived category of analytic module sheaves. Compare the ambient tensor and RHom of the realized inputs; finite-Tor boundedness receipts and realization isomorphisms identify the bounded restrictions. Over complex coefficient fields, use their separate analytic boundedness theorem, not a universal bounded operation over arbitrary rings.

nodes.title: Algebraic traces and cycle classes versus topological orientation
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth separated of pure dimension d over ℂ and Λ = ℤ/n, ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ. Under the comparison isomorphism H^q(X_ét, Λ) ≅ H^q(X^an, Λ) (EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison) and the identification Λ(1) ≅ Λ given by exp(2πi/n) ↦ 1 (ζ_n ↦ 1): (a) the étale trace Tr : H^{2d}_c(X_ét, Λ(d)) → Λ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11) corresponds to integration against the complex orientation, Tr_X ↦ ∫_{X^an}, sending the class of a point to 1; (b) the étale cycle class cl(Z) ∈ H^{2r}(X_ét, Λ(r)) of a closed subvariety of codimension r corresponds to the topological fundamental class of Z^an (Poincaré dual of [Z^an]); (c) cup products and compactly supported duality pairings correspond. The sign convention: c₁(O(1)) on P¹ maps to the positive generator of H²(P¹(ℂ), ℤ) for the complex orientation, with the Kummer sequence matched to the exponential sequence by exp(2πi·/n).
hypotheses: X smooth over ℂ; the identification Λ(1) ≅ Λ through e^{2πi/n} is part of the statement (other choices change Tr by a sign or a unit).
proofSteps: Use the analytic Kummer sequence and exp(2πi·) with the same positive root-of-unity coordinates. The Kummer connecting cocycle is the exponential integral Chern cocycle modulo n. ComplexComparisonPartII §C5.4 already identifies the integral analytic class with the topological c₁, and §C6.3 fixes the positive Kummer generator on G_m. The residue here is the commutative Kummer/exponential connecting square and its trace/Gysin normalization, as in BBD 6.1.4, pp.151–152.

Traces are normalized by points and c₁(O(1)) on P¹ (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.11, ClassicalAlgebraic.smoothTrace, whose P¹ check sends c₁(O(1)) to 1), and the topological integration satisfies the same normalization; both are compatible with Gysin maps of points, so they agree.

Cycle classes: both sides are determined by the fundamental class of the smooth locus and semi-purity (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/cycle-class-map; the localized classes of regular immersions are EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.9).
acceptance: X = P¹: Tr(c₁(O(1))) = 1 on both sides (the stage's acceptance: P¹'s orientation).
X a connected smooth open curve: H²_c(X, Λ(1)) ≅ Λ with the same normalization.
A smooth divisor D ⊂ X: cl(D) = c₁(O(D)) maps to the topological Poincaré dual of [D] under both routes.

nodes.title: Betti numbers of smooth complete intersections are independent of the field
nodes.statement: Fix N, m and a multidegree (d_1, …, d_{N−m}). For every separably closed field k of characteristic ≠ ℓ and every smooth complete intersection X ⊂ P^N_k of that multidegree and dimension m, every Betti number is independent of the geometric field, and dim H^m(X, ℚ_ℓ) equals the topological Betti number b_m(X_ℂ^an) of any smooth complete intersection X_ℂ ⊂ P^N_ℂ of the same multidegree, and hence the primitive rank b_m^0 = dim H^m(X, ℚ_ℓ)_0 of EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology is a function of (N, m, d_•) only; for a smooth hypersurface of degree d, b_m^0 = ((d − 1)^{m+2} + (−1)^m(d − 1))/d.
hypotheses: Smooth complete intersections of a fixed multidegree; ℓ invertible in k.
m≥1 for the primitive-rank and displayed hypersurface formula, as in EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology; d≥1. Zero-dimensional reduced cohomology is a different convention.
proofSteps: The parameter scheme S ⊂ ∏ P(Sym^{d_i}) over Spec ℤ[1/ℓ] of tuples defining a smooth complete intersection of dimension m is open with geometrically irreducible (hence connected) fibres and nonempty over every point; the universal family f : 𝒳 → S is smooth and proper (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0).

Smooth proper base change makes R^mf_*ℚ_ℓ lisse on the connected parameter scheme (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3, VanishingCycles.lisseDirectImageTransport, at finite levels, then §F.4), hence its rank is constant. Identifications of different geometric fibres require a choice of path or specialization data; the canonical conclusion here is equality of ranks, not a canonical identification of all fibres.

Over ℂ, Artin's comparison (EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison) identifies dim H^m(X_ℂ, ℚ_ℓ) with the topological Betti number. The hypersurface formula: by étale Gauss–Bonnet (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.6, VanishingCycles.etaleGaussBonnet) χ(X) = deg c_m(T_X), and c(T_X) = (1+h)^{N+1}∏(1+d_ih)^{−1} restricted to X (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5); EDC.4/complete-intersection-cohomology gives all other Betti numbers, so b_m is determined by χ.
acceptance: Smooth plane cubics: b_1 = 2 over every k (= (8 − 2)/3 = 2 by the formula with m = 1, d = 3).
Smooth quadric surfaces: b_2^0 = (1 + 1)/2 = 1.
Further values of the hypersurface formula, checked in the suggested file: conic 0, cubic surface 6, quartic surface 21, quintic threefold 204 (b₃ = 204).

sources.match: Milne: the primitive rank depends only on m and the degrees, with the explicit hypersurface formula.

§F.3 states lissity of R^if_* for smooth proper f with finite lisse coefficients; §F.6 states étale Gauss–Bonnet deg c_d(T_X) = Σ(−1)^i dim H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ) for smooth proper X over an algebraically closed field.

nodes.title: Transport of duality and perversity statements to diamonds in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let k be of characteristic p, X separated of finite type over k, and Λ torsion killed by an integer prime to p. Put a : X → Spec k, B = (Spec k)^◇, and K_{X^◇/B} = a^{◇!}c_{Spec k}^*Λ. For K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ), ECD 27.2–27.4 imply Rc_{X*}K_{X^◇/B} ≅ K_X and Rc_{X*}RHom(c_X^*K, K_{X^◇/B}) ≅ D_XK. These recover scheme duality through the right adjoint. The stronger assertions c_X^*K_X ≅ K_{X^◇/B} and c_X^*D_XK ≅ D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K are conditional on an additional exceptional-pullback/internal-Hom comparison and preservation of the essential image; these inputs are not supplied by 27.1–27.4. No perverse t-structure on arbitrary diamonds is asserted.
hypotheses: Characteristic p, finite-type separated X over k, torsion coefficients prime to p; the dualizing complex is relative to B = (Spec k)^◇.

The strong pullback transport requested by the stage remains a recorded gap of the accepted EDC.6 packet (gap “Strong diamond exceptional-pullback and internal-Hom transport”, with its AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3 request); this node proves only right-adjoint recovery.

The Rc_* identities live in the unbounded etale derived category. A bounded constructible K enters through its etale realization; no preservation of D^b_c by Rc_* on arbitrary diamond objects is assumed. The relative dualizing objects on both sides use their actual maps to the common base.

Tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change are the enhanced operations of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3 in the ambient unbounded derived category; the scheme dualizing complex, biduality and exchange isomorphisms are EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.5. Bounded outputs require actual bounded-constructible restriction witnesses.
proofSteps: Use R a^! Rc_{Spec k*} ≅ Rc_{X*}R a^{◇!} and Rc_{Spec k*}c_{Spec k}^*Λ ≅ Λ to recover K_X.
Apply the internal-Hom right-adjoint identity of 27.3 with first input c_X^*K, then the unit K ≅ Rc_{X*}c_X^*K to obtain D_XK.
A counit c_X^*Rc_{X*}D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K → D_{X^◇/B}c_X^*K need not be an isomorphism by full faithfulness alone; the missing essential-image argument is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: For X=𝔸^d, Rc_{X*}K_{(𝔸^d)^◇/B} ≅ Λ(d)[2d], and Rc_{X*}RHom(c_X^*Λ,K_{X^◇/B}) gives the same scheme dualizing complex.
For X=P¹, right-adjoint recovery gives Λ(1)[2]. Strong c^* transport on either example remains conditional on the additional L3 theorem; these checks assert no unconditional counit isomorphism.
